en: *The Ritual for the Recitation of the Benevolent Kings’ Prajñāpāramitā*,
one fascicle. Compiled by the Grand Marshal of the Court, Peer of the Third Rank, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Duke of Sui with a fief of three thousand households, recipient of the purple robe, and posthumously honored as Minister of Education.

Translated by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, Tripitaka Master of the Great Xingshan Monastery, who was posthumously titled Dajian and Grandly Honored as Dayangzhi, by Imperial Decree. At that time, the Buddha addressed King Prasenajit.
I shall now explain for Your Majesty the vidyā-dhāraṇī method of the *Prajñāpāramitā* for Benevolent Kings who Protect the State.
Your Majesty should receive this with careful attention and listen with single-minded devotion.
First, I shall clarify the ritual procedures for entering the maṇḍala.
If any benevolent kings seek to pacify calamities,
they must first bathe and don fresh, clean garments;
if they are kings who practice the Dharma, they should receive the upavāsa precepts.
One should give rise to a profound and reverent mind for the Mahāyāna.
Desiring to achieve accomplishment, one should not begrudge even body or life.
One should extensively arouse a heart of compassionate vows to deliver infinite sentient beings. Those who can act in this way will swiftly attain accomplishment.

Having entered the dharma hall, prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground and pay homage to all the Triple Gem throughout the entire dharma realm. With the right knee touching the ground, repent for all karmic obstacles of the three types of action.
I exhort the Buddhas of the ten directions to turn the wheel of the true Dharma;
I entreat all Tathāgatas to remain long in the world;
and I rejoice in the merit and wisdom cultivated by those of the three vehicles.
By means of all the merit I, [Name], have cultivated,
I dedicate it entirely toward unexcelled bodhi.
May it be shared with all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma realm.
The siddhis sought shall be swiftly and fully attained.
Next, assume the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
Should one lack the necessary conditions and be unable to bathe, [one may proceed as follows].
With both hands applying the fragrant unguent, generate a mind of earnest devotion and form the Seal of Purity (*viśuddhi-mudrā*).
With palms joined hollowly at the heart like an unfurled lotus flower, recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarva-dharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’haṃ. Recite this mantra three times.
While reciting, direct the mind to pervade universally:
"All phenomena are originally pure;
therefore, my own body is also entirely pure."
He then closed his eyes and focused his mind,
visualizing all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas within their assemblies at the sites of enlightenment filling the entirety of space,
holding various kinds of exquisite incense and flowers.
With the utmost sincerity of the three karmas, prostrate with the head to pay homage.
First, the Binding of the Buddha Family Samaya Seal: Hold both hands at the heart.
Crossing the hands inside, form fists and extend both thumbs upward. Recite the mantra:
Oṃ īna īka svāhā. Recite this mantra three times without making a sound.
The same applies to all subsequent sections.
One scatters [the flowers] upon the crown of the head;
by binding this mudrā and reciting this Buddha-family samaya mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
All Buddhas of the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm gather like clouds, filling the void,
and empower the practitioner to be free from all obstacles and afflictions.
Through the purity of the three karmas, may the practices and vows swiftly attain accomplishment.
2. Binding the Samaya Seal of the Bodhisattva Family: Second, for binding the Samaya Seal of the Bodhisattva Family, place both hands at the heart as before and form fists.
Bend the left thumb into the palm and recite the mantra:
Oṃ āruṇika svāhā. Recite this three times as before.
By scattering [flowers] upon the crown of the head while binding this mudrā and reciting these samaya mantras of the various bodhisattva families,
one immediately attains the presence of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and the others.
All Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm gathered like clouds, filling the void,
and empowered the practitioner of this ritual method so that their three karmas became pure and free from all calamities; for these Bodhisattvas had undertaken their original vows of compassion.
May all that is sought be completely fulfilled. 3.
Binding the Samaya Seal of the Vajra Family, Part Three: To bind the Samaya Seal of the Vajra Family, form the seal as before with the right hand, and extend the left thumb.
Bend the right thumb into the palm.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajra-dhṛk svāhā. As before, recite it three times and scatter [the mudrā] over the crown of the head.
By binding this mudrā and reciting the Vajra Family Samaya mantra,
one immediately causes all the vajras of the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm to manifest in bodies of wrathful majesty.
Gathering like clouds to fill the realm of empty space,
they empower the practitioner of the ritual practice so that their three karmas become as firm and solid as vajra.
That is to say, those noble ones, by virtue of the Buddha’s majestic power and through the force of their own vows,
protect and sustain the national realm on a large scale so that no calamities or disasters occur,
and on a small scale, they ensure that even a single person is free from all misfortunes.
4. The Fourth Seal for Protecting the Body: Furthermore, one should employ the mudrās bound by the three families and empower the five places by reciting the mantras.
That is to say, at the five locations— the forehead, the left shoulder, the right shoulder, the heart, and the throat—
one scatters [the syllables] above the crown of the head;
thus one becomes armored in the adamantine, firm mail.

By means of this empowerment, the body of the Wandering One blazes with such majestic radiance that all māras who create obstacles and afflictions do not dare to look upon him with their eyes, but flee in haste.

5. Binding the Sealing Gesture for Expelling Obstacles and the Precious Boundary of the Vajra Directions. Fifth: Binding the Sealing Gesture for Expelling Obstacles and the Precious Boundary of the Vajra Directions. To the right, one uses the aforementioned mudrā of the Vajra Family.
Reciting that mantra, circumambulate the maṇḍala three times to the left;
this will immediately expel all powerful māras who follow the Buddha and Bodhisattvas,
causing those who remain hidden to flee far away to other realms.
Circumambulating three times to the right according to the size of one's mind,
this immediately constitutes the adamantine square boundary of jewels (*vajra-caturaśra-ratna-sīmā*),
which even all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not transgress.
How much more so for those who create obstacles and afflictions, who will find no opportunity [to harm];
he shall scatter them from the crown of his head.
Sixth: The Seal for Invoking the Assembly of Sages to Descend upon the Altar. For the right [hand], employ the three mudrās of the preceding divisions and recite the mantras.
With the thumb, beckon toward oneself three times; thus,
the holy beings of the three families who previously filled the sky [arrive].
Each remains in its own position without obstructing one another, abiding in stillness;
then [the water] is scattered upon the crown of the head.
7. The Seventh Seal for Offering Arghya Fragrant Water: For the seal of offering arghya fragrant water, hold a maṇi-jewel vessel filled with fragrant water with both hands, supporting it from below.
Place it between the eyebrows and recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajranāga hūṃ. Recite this three times while extending the mind to pervade [the area].
In succession, they bathe all the noble assembly and scatter [the water] upon their heads;
by virtue of this offering of argha, [the merit is attained].
From the stage of practice through aspiration up to the stage of the cloud of dharma,
throughout each and every stage, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm provide their protective empowerment and confer the empowerment of all Buddhas.
8. The Eighth Seal for Offering the Precious Throne: For the seal for offering the precious throne, place both hands at the heart with palms joined in the hollowed gesture (*śūnyamudrā*).
The two thumbs and the two little fingers [are then extended].
The two thumbs are slightly bent against each other,
while the remaining six fingers are spread apart and slightly curved like blossoming lotus flowers.
The mantra is: Oṃ kamala svāhā. By forming the mudrā and reciting this mantra, the precious throne offered shall be accepted and utilized by all the noble assembly exactly as it is.
This causes those who practice the Dharma to reach the stage of fruition and obtain a vajra-solid jewel throne. Ninth:
Binding the Seal of Universal Offering. To bind the seal of universal offering, join the two hands in *añjali* with the right hand on top.
Interlace the five fingers with the right pressing over the left, place them at the heart, and recite the mantra:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ svāhā khaṃ unagati-sphara hīṃ gagaṇe jaḥ svāhā*. By binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra, the lotus-heart spreads wide.
Pervading the ocean-like assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas throughout the entire Dharma-realm,
one universally rains down all manner of offerings.
First, recite this once.
Recite the second time: "Countless sand-like jeweled vessels are filled with ointments, which are universally applied to the assembly of noble ones.
Various flower garlands universally adorn them."
Recite for the third time.
Burn various kinds of incense as a universal offering.
Recite for the fourth time.
Raining down the most exquisite food and drink among all the heavens,
they place them in precious vessels and offer them universally.
Recite this for the fifth time.
They rain down various maṇi jewels as lamps to provide universal offerings.
Through the power of the empowerment of reciting the mantras,
the incense and other offerings presented reach all the assemblies in the oceans of worlds, where they are truly enjoyed by the assembly of noble ones.
Those who practice the Dharma will constantly obtain this retribution in future lives. 10.
The Tenth: Binding the Fundamental Seal of the Prajñāpāramitā. To bind the fundamental seal of the Prajñāpāramitā, again place the backs of both hands together.
Draw back the two index fingers;
bend the two little fingers into the palms;
and press the tips of the two index fingers with the thumbs respectively.
Place it upon the heart.
Recite the dhāraṇī from within the sūtra seven times;
by forming this mudrā and reciting the dhāraṇī, [the merit is attained].
The practitioner of the Dharma practice themselves immediately transforms into the Bodhisattva Prajñāpāramitā,
who serves as the mother of all Buddhas.
This Bodhisattva image sits in the full lotus posture upon a white lotus flower.
His body is the color of golden light,
adorned all over with necklaces and ornaments of various jewels;
upon his head he wears a jeweled crown, bound with white silk ribbons.
Both shoulders hang down.
Her left hand is held at the heart holding a Prajñāpāramitā manuscript,
and her right hand is at the breast forming the *dharmacakra-mudrā* (teaching gesture).
Press the tip of the ring finger with the thumb,
and immediately visualize light flowing from the crown of the head down to the feet through all the pores of the Bodhisattva’s body, manifesting in various colors.
Pervading the entire Dharma-realm,
within each and every ray of light, they manifest immeasurable Buddhas throughout all worlds across the realm of empty space.

Having contemplated thus, King Dharmarāja, who dwells in samādhi and practices the Dharma, universally proclaimed for all sentient beings, according to their faculties, the profound Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā, causing them all to realize and understand it.
Perform the mudrā of scattering upon the crown of the head.
Hold a rosary in the palms of the hands and join them at the heart.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ virujanamala svāhā. Recite this three times; having empowered the rosary, place it upon the crown of your head.
Thereafter, one should focus the mind:
with the left hand supporting the beads, the right hand moves them,
maintaining moment-to-moment correspondence while abiding in the Samādhi of the Mother of Buddhas.
Contemplate the mind without interruption.
Recite one hundred and eight times, or twenty-one times.
The mantra to be recited is as follows:
Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya. Namo ’ryāya.
5. Samantabhadraya | 6. Mṛtidāntāya | 7. Mahāsattvāya | 8.
Mahākāruṇikāya | 9. Tadyathā | 10. Jñānaprati... (The text appears to be a fragment of a mantra.)
11. *nirvāraya* (close/ward off), 12. *pratiṣṭhāpaya* (establish/settle), 13.
*sarvabuddhāvalokite* (O you who behold all Buddhas), 14. *yogapariniṣpanne* (O you who are perfected in yoga), 15.
*jñānarūpagate* (O you who have entered the form of gnosis).
Ṣaṭ-tri-ya-tva 17, pariniṣpanna 18, mṛti-jita-sañjanani 19, sarva-vyādhi-viśodhaya 20, dharma-sāgara-pratītya 21, a... 22.
Mukhaśirovane (22) mahāsamantabhadrapūjite (23) nairātmye (24) vikaraṇi (25) paripūrṇi (26) sa... (27)
Vasita (27) | Namaḥ siddhe (28) | Sarvabodhisattva (29) | Sañjanani (30) | Bhagavati (31) | Buddhamate (32) | Ārāṇi kāraṇi (33) ||
33. Araṇakāraṇe | 34. Mahāpracaṇḍa | 35. Pramiti svāhā | 36. Thus, one should recite and contemplate with a sincere mind as previously described.
Once the prescribed number of recitations is complete,
one should place the rosary upon the crown of the head and set it back in its original location.
Then, forming the *samādhi-mudrā*, extend both hands horizontally with the right hand pressing down upon the left.
Place it below the navel.
With the body upright and eyes closed, the head slightly bent, focus intently on the heart.
Contemplate clearly the Mirror-like Wisdom (ādarśa-jñāna), which is perfectly luminous and measures one cubit in length and breadth.
Gradually pervading the entire dharma-realm,
one contemplates the arrangement of the characters in a rightward spiral sequence,
with the radiant light of each individual character penetrating and illuminating all.
From the outside toward the inside, one proceeds to the syllable *dha*;
from the inside toward the outside, one gradually contemplates each syllable,
beginning again and again in a continuous cycle.
Upon reaching the third repetition, the mind becomes well-settled in tranquility;
one clearly and distinctly contemplates the meaning of what is expressed:
that all things are equal, being neither born nor extinguished.
Pervading the entire dharma-realm, it is neither moving nor still;
with concentration and wisdom functioning in tandem, it is forever free from all signs.
This is precisely the samādhi-contemplation of Prajñāpāramitā.
From this point, one should instead form the seal of the *prajñāpāramitā*,
recite the dhāraṇī seven times,
and scatter it over the crown of the head.
Next, bind the seal of universal offering.
As before, direct the mind and perform the offerings in sequence before the assembly of noble ones.
With all the merit produced by the practices previously cultivated,
one shall entirely dedicate it to support and fulfill all sought-after aspirations,
for the sake of the nation, the family, and the complete benefit of others.
Thereafter, one dedicates [the merit] to sentient beings;
one dedicates it toward the adornment and purification of the Buddha-land; one dedicates it toward the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*);
and one dedicates it toward the pursuit of unsurpassed enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
May all sentient beings together swiftly reach the other shore.
Next, bind the previously mentioned boundary-binding mudrā;
recite the previous mantra three times while turning to the left, whereby the boundary is dissolved.
Next, bind the seals of the three preceding families and recite the previous mantra three times;
in each case, flick the thumbs outward.
Thereupon, the assembly of noble beings is dismissed, each returning to their own original land.
The practitioner prostrates and departs,
performing circumambulation as usual.
One should uphold, recite, and chant the Mahāyāna without allowing the mind to become distracted.
Thus, from the fifth watch until dawn constitutes the first period;
from after midday until the hour of Wei (the seventh watch) constitutes the second period.
From after dusk until midnight constitutes the third period;
from after midnight until five o'clock in the morning constitutes the fourth period.
In these periods, each follows its respective original count.
Through diligent effort without indolence, all external enemies will naturally submit,
and all calamities shall never arise again.
At that time, King Prasenajit, having heard what the Buddha had said, [was filled with joy].
Immediately rising from their seats, they prostrated themselves, circumambulated [the Buddha],
and with joyful exultation, received and practiced it with faith.
*The Ritual for the Recitation of the Benevolent Kings’ Prajñāpāramitā*, one fascicle.
